sovereign_country.strategic_role: 非洲第一大金融枢纽、辐射南部非洲关税同盟（SACU）商贸

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Retail Sale via Internet - DTC Brand Webstore

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: South Africa (Republic of South Africa; unitary national jurisdiction, no sub-state company registry distinction)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: SA-UK Double Taxation Agreement (in force; dividends, interest and royalties relief for e-commerce income)
SA-Mauritius Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (in force; commonly used inbound investment treaty addressing capital gains on share disposals)
SA-China Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (2001, in force; applicable to royalties and services income streams of a Shopify DTC brand)
SACU Agreement, 2002 (Southern African Customs Union; common external tariff and preferential regional market access)
AfCFTA Agreement (South Africa is a founding signatory, ratified 2018; trade in goods, services and digital trade disciplines)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008 (ss. 13-19, 40, 66-67); Companies Regulations, 2011; Income Tax Act 58 of 1962; Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), an agency of the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a (Pty) Ltd; 100 ordinary shares at a nominal subscription of ZAR 1.00 each are fully subscribed by the founding directors. No escrow account is mandated by the Companies Act. Share consideration must comply with s. 40 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, unanimously, as follows: (1) The allotment and issue of 100 ordinary shares, at a subscription price of ZAR 1.00 each, to the founding subscribers, is hereby approved and recorded. (2) The registered office and principal place of business shall be [Street Address, City] and shall be filed with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission accordingly. (3) [Director Name] is appointed as initial sole director; [Officer Name] as chief executive officer; and [Officer Name] as public officer for tax purposes, each to act until the next annual general meeting. (4) Management authority to open the company's bank account and execute all related mandates is delegated to the directors. Adopted and signed this [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online name reservation application on the CIPC portal, verify that the proposed name is not confusingly similar or undesirable, pay the statutory name reservation fee, and retain the reservation reference number. The reservation remains valid for six months.
required_dossiers: Completed name reservation application (Form CoR 9.1)
Certified copy of the applicant's identity document or passport
Consent letter from any entity or individual whose name is incorporated into the proposed name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC refuses the name as undesirable or confusingly similar, file an amended name reservation promptly or elect to incorporate using the company registration number as the formal name, and lodge an appeal or objection in terms of the Companies Regulations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft the Memorandum of Incorporation and Notice of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services Company Registration workflow with legal drafting support
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the MOI adopting the standard form and including bespoke provisions for authorised share capital, director powers, and quorum requirements. Complete Form CoR 14.1 (Notice of Incorporation) with the proposed company details. Signatures of domestic subscribers may be witnessed; foreign signatories require notarisation and apostille.
required_dossiers: Drafted Memorandum of Incorporation setting out share capital and governance rules
Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1)
Consents to act of each initial director
Certified copies of the identity documents or passports of all subscribers and directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC issues a documentation query or compliance notice, revise the MOI or CoR 14.1 and resubmit through the portal within the statutory cure period, paying any applicable resubmission fee before the application lapses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit the Incorporation Application and Pay the Filing Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services online filing portal or an accredited service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the completed Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1) and the executed MOI to the CIPC portal, verify the registered address and director declarations, pay the incorporation fee electronically, and retain the payment receipt together with the submission acknowledgement.
required_dossiers: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1)
Executed Memorandum of Incorporation
Directors' consents to act and declarations of eligibility
Proof of payment of the CIPC incorporation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected for defects, CIPC issues a notice of non-compliance; remedy the stated deficiency within 20 business days of the notice or re-file the application, ensuring corrected documents are certified before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain the Certificate of Incorporation and Registration Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, download the electronic Certificate of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.3) from the CIPC portal. Verify the legal name, registration number, date of incorporation, and company type. Circulate the certificate to directors, SARS, banks, and advisors.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.3)
Final registered Memorandum of Incorporation
CIPC transaction reference and payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains a material error, file a rectification application with CIPC supported by an affidavit and the correct particulars; the Commission may correct the record upon satisfaction that no third-party rights are prejudiced.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Income Tax, VAT, PAYE, UIF and SDL with SARS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) eFiling portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as a taxpayer for Income Tax, appoint a public officer within one month of incorporation, and complete VAT registration (mandatory if taxable turnover exceeds ZAR 1,000,000; voluntary where turnover exceeds ZAR 50,000). Register for PAYE, UIF, and SDL if employees will be hired, and note the DTC e-commerce model for correct turnover declarations.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.3)
Memorandum of Incorporation
Identity documents and SARS registration details of directors and the appointed public officer
Bank account confirmation or registered office address proof
Estimated annual turnover declaration for VAT purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS returns a status mismatch or requests verification documents, respond within 21 days through eFiling with certified supporting records; escalate to the SARS branch office or tax practitioner if the account remains inactive beyond the SLA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Beneficial Ownership and Apply for Municipal Trading Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC Beneficial Ownership Filing Module and the relevant metropolitan or local municipality
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the register of beneficial owners with CIPC in the prescribed format, identifying all individuals who control the company. Concurrently, apply to the local municipality for a home occupation or general trading licence covering the e-commerce administrative and dispatch premises, submitting the signed lease or ownership title.
required_dossiers: Beneficial ownership declaration form identifying ultimate natural persons
Certified identity documents or passports of each beneficial owner
Municipal business trading or home occupation licence application
Proof of premises (lease agreement or title deed)
Certificate of Incorporation and MOI extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC queries the beneficial ownership filing, reconcile controlling-interest declarations and resubmit within the prescribed period. If the municipality refuses the trading licence, appeal to the municipal licensing appeal board under the applicable by-laws with evidence of zoning compliance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal Business Regulation and Licensing Unit of the applicable local authority, with oversight by the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: General Trading Licence / Home Occupation Certificate for E-Commerce Retail (ISIC 4791) under the Municipal By-Laws

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) and the competent provincial environmental authority under NEMA Act 107 of 1998
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 - Low-risk registration / exemption for pure online retail without manufacturing; a full Environmental Impact Assessment is not required unless warehousing or dispatch facilities exceed Listing Notice 3 thresholds (e.g., floor area exceeding 1,000 m2 or location within sensitive environmental buffers).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process water discharge from DTC operations; domestic wastewater must comply with local municipal sewer discharge limits. Packaging waste must comply with the Extended Producer Responsibility Regulations, 2021 under the National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008, requiring registration of the importer or online retailer as a packaging producer. No VOC-emission equipment is used or permitted without registered air emission control.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the local fire authority for any warehouse or office premise; structural occupancy clearance confirming building load and safe egress; compliance with the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 including a health and safety file, and registration with the Compensation Fund (COIDA) where employees are engaged.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) – eFiling online portal (www.sarsefiling.co.za)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Non-resident company must first apply for a SARS income tax reference number and VAT number via SARS eFiling using a SARS-registered tax practitioner or through the non-resident electronic registration channel. Submit certified Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum of Incorporation, proof of registered foreign address, resolution appointing a local public officer, financial statements or certain projections, and evidence of South African business activity. Once VAT registration is approved, the enterprise must file VAT returns on eFiling and maintain a local public officer for SARS correspondence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists. South Africa applies entity-level income tax. Relevant elections include: VAT grouping election under Section 50 of the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991; hybrid mismatch elective treatment under Sections 8K and 8L of the Income Tax Act 58 of 1962; and CFC high-tax exemption election under Section 9D(9E) where the foreign subsidiary is subject to a minimum effective tax rate.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory registration where taxable supplies exceed or are likely to exceed ZAR 1,000,000 (R1 million) in a consecutive 12-month period; voluntary registration threshold ZAR 50,000. Non-resident suppliers of electronic services cross this compulsory threshold if turnover exceeds ZAR 1,000,000 globally.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Africa currently maintains no real-time electronic invoice clearance or digital stamping mandate. A VAT-registered supplier must issue tax invoices satisfying Section 20 of the VAT Act, or simplified invoices under Section 21 for amounts below ZAR 5,000, and submit electronic VAT returns via SARS eFiling. SARS publishes an API framework for accredited software integrators, but no mandatory continuous transaction control (CTC) or fiscal data stamping is in force.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under Section 11(1)(a) for goods physically exported from South Africa where the supplier obtains documentary proof in the required form. Services are zero-rated under Section 11(2)(l) where they are supplied to a non-resident and the direct benefit occurs outside South Africa; related intellectual property and logistics services may be zero-rated only if specific statutory conditions are met. The supplier must be a registered VAT vendor and must retain evidence before the zero rate is applied.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Inward Remittance Certificate or bank proof of payment in foreign currency
Proof of delivery/customs entry at destination
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS audits export zero-rating strictly. If export documentation is incomplete, untimely, or fraudulent, the zero rate is reversed and VAT becomes payable, together with interest calculated from the original due date and an understatement penalty under Section 223 of the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011 of up to 150% of the shortfall for intentional misstatement; deliberate evasion may additionally trigger criminal prosecution.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) - Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), acting under the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961, promulgated under the Currency and Exchanges Act 9 of 1933, in consultation with National Treasury; implementation is conducted through authorised dealers (commercial banks) appointed by FinSurv.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Rand (ZAR) is freely convertible for current-account transactions (trade in goods and services, interest, dividends) without prior SARB approval, while capital-account inflows from non-residents are liberalised; outward capital transfers by residents, external borrowing above prescribed thresholds, and certain structured derivative transactions remain subject to FinSurv approval or authorised-dealer reporting. Profit remittance via dividend distribution to non-resident shareholders is freely remittable provided the dividend is declared out of distributable profits under the Companies Act 71 of 2008, is subject to 20% (or treaty-reduced) Dividend Withholding Tax, and is supported by board minutes, audited/reviewed annual financial statements or management accounts, and evidence of non-resident status; no 'blocked rand' or standing prior-approval obstacle applies to a standard DTC e-commerce company.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the SARB Currency and Exchanges Manual for Exporters (2023 revision) and FinSurv enforcement policy, export proceeds must be received in South Africa within 30 days from the date of export (reduced from the former 180-day requirement in the 2021 reform). On receipt, proceeds must either be credited to a domestic ZAR account (triggering full conversion) or be retained without mandatory conversion in an approved Foreign Currency Account (FCA) held with an authorised dealer; there is no partial surrender ratio in the classic sense, but the practical obligation is 100% repatriation within the 30-day window, with 100% conversion to ZAR if the exporter elects not to maintain an FCA, and continued FCA retention remains subject to authorised-dealer oversight, FinSurv reporting, and the AD's internal credit limits.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: First National Bank (a division of FirstRand Bank Limited)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: ZAR Operational Business Account; Foreign Currency Account (FCA) for export receipts; Capital Escrow Account for retained inbound equity funding

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: The Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: ZAR Operational Settlement Account; Export Proceeds FCA; supplementary trade-finance and Import/Export Guarantee facilities
ZAR Business Current Account; FCA sub-ledger for cross-border e-commerce receipts; documentary trade desk for LC and open-account settlements
ZAR Operational Account; FCA and corporate currency account with integrated FX hedging lines
Corporate Treasury Account with private-bank-style FX execution and FCA wrapper; suited to higher-value DTC treasury structures

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium - feasible as a supplementary offshore receivable-concentration rail, but not as a replacement for a domestic authorised-dealer bank account. Airwallex, Wise Business and Payoneer are not licensed authorised dealers in South Africa under the Exchange Control Regulations, cannot lawfully settle ZAR current-account obligations, and cannot perform FinSurv reporting. Legal constraints are: (i) a resident (Pty) Ltd must receive export proceeds through a South African authorised dealer for the 30-day repatriation rule; (ii) ZAR payouts flowing through an unlicensed EMI without an underlying AD transaction risk exchange-control circumvention; (iii) the entity may use EMIs to warehouse USD/EUR receipts from Shopify Payouts offshore only if the funds are subsequently remitted to the SA authorised dealer within the statutory timeline and a complete digital documentation trail is retained.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: De facto physical presence mandate: under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 (FICA) and FIC Compliance Directives, South African Tier-1 banks require an in-person 'fit and proper' interview with at least one executive director, the authorised representative and the natural-person ultimate beneficial owner(s), supported by original or commissioner-of-oaths-certified identity documents and a board resolution for account opening. Fully remote onboarding is technically possible under FIC Directive 5 (2021) where banks deploy an approved biometric eKYC provider, but in practice the major ADs still require a physical or notarially-certified appearance for a company with non-resident shareholders; foreign directors may instead arrange a sworn affidavit before a South African-registered commissioner of oaths or notary where the bank's risk committee accepts it.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: 'Shell or substance-deficient entity' - new (Pty) Ltd with no physical premises, no payroll, and no audited financial history
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Operating-substance bundle comprising CIPC registration transcript, signed lease or virtual-office contract for the registered physical address, Shopify storefront URL and latest 90-day payout statements, supplier agreements and invoices, advertising and fulfilment contracts (e.g., 3PL), customer-support logs, and a draft risk-management matrix evidencing going-concern operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: 'UBO opacity or divergence from the CIPC beneficial-ownership register' - nominee shareholding or a foreign trust in the ownership chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CIPC Beneficial Ownership Register transcript, memorandum of incorporation, share register and share certificates, signed UBO declaration by each natural-person owner under section 56 of the Companies Act and FIC Guidance Note 7A, together with source-of-funds documentation (bank statements, sale agreement, or tax clearance) for every shareholder holding 5% or more.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: 'Source of initial capital injection from a personal offshore account' - inbound equity remittance disproportionate to declared income
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share-subscription agreement, board resolution authorising the share issue, CIPC notice of share issue lodged within the statutory period, notarised bank statements of the remitting account for six months, certified source-of-wealth narrative (savings, prior dividends, inheritance, asset sale), SARS tax clearance or taxpayer PIN, and a transaction-tracing worksheet mapping the SWIFT MT103 to the subscription payment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: 'Sanctions, PEP or high-risk jurisdiction screening hit' - director or UBO name matching UN/OFAC/EU/South African sanctions lists, or prior PEP exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Screening release letter from the bank's compliance team, notarised non-PEP/non-sanctions declaration by each director and UBO, forensic sanctions-list comparison report, CIPC and passport extracts, a legal opinion from South African counsel on beneficial ownership, and a cleaned adverse-media research file supported by court or discharge documents where relevant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: 'High-risk e-commerce fingerprint' - elevated chargeback velocity, crypto-adjacent payment flows, or affiliate-network routing inconsistent with the declared Shopify DTC model
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform-generated reporting pack including Shopify Payments/PayPal/Stripe settlement statements, chargeback-to-transaction ratio report evidencing a below-1% threshold, verified bank-account confirmation on the processor dashboard, fulfilment and logistics tracking samples, and a documented rationale for any multi-channel checkout or subscription-billing feature.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing: wire funds via SWIFT MT103 from the non-resident shareholder's bank to the company's ZAR corporate account at the South African authorised dealer, stating purpose code 'EQ - Direct investment: equity' (IMF BOP classification / SARB EDP code 10.02) and referencing the company registration number. The AD requires the MOI, board resolution approving the issue, share-subscription agreement, and source-of-funds verification; no prior SARB approval is needed for an inbound equity contribution, but the company must issue the shares and file the CIPC notice of issue under section 40 of the Companies Act within the prescribed period, and the AD will report the inward transfer to FinSurv and IMF BOP statistics. A FICA cash-threshold report is not triggered by wire transfers, but a FIC report may arise on unexplained counterparty anomalies or associated cash deposits.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for open-account trade settlements and supplier payments against invoices; (ii) SWIFT MT700 (irrevocable documentary Letter of Credit at sight or usance) for purchase-order or bulk-restock transactions, with shipping documents and bill of entry presented through the AD's trade desk; (iii) SWIFT MT202 COV for interbank settlement of third-party currency payments; (iv) domestic ZAR EFT (BankservAfrica eFT) and PayShap instant payments for local fulfilment and DTC refunds; (v) cross-border acquiring and Shopify payout conversion to ZAR via the AD's auto-conversion or FCA-based FX conversion. Each outbound payment must be coded with the correct EDP trade purpose code (goods import or services) and, where applicable, supported by a SARS bill of entry and import documentation for customs reconciliation under the Customs and Excise Act 91 of 1964.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward Exchange Contract (FEC) with the authorised dealer - permitted for firm and reasonably anticipated trade-related foreign-currency exposures (export receivables and import payables) up to 12 months' tenor, extendable by the AD with documented business rationale under the classic SARB trade-cover regime.

Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) - permitted onshore only where the ZAR leg can be documented as a hedge of foreign-currency cash flows and the counterparty is a bank; a FinSurv-approved authorised dealer must handle ZAR settlement, and the entity should evidence the underlying Shopify/PayPal receivable being hedged.

Cross-Currency Swap (CCS) - permissible through the authorised dealer for balance-sheet hedging of multi-year external loan or reinvestment exposures (e.g., USD/ZAR or EUR/ZAR), subject to internal AD product approval and, where the tenor exceeds standard trade-cover horizons, to FinSurv approval or AD delegated authority.

FX Option (put/call, premium settled in ZAR) - authorised for hedging anticipated trade flows where the AD confirms the premium is economically attributable to South African residency; delta-limited structures (zero-premium collars and participating forwards) are permissible with an approved underlying exposure.

Nostro/Vostro account offset and multi-currency netting through the AD's treasury desk - used as an intraday liquidity hedge for multi-currency Shopify payout cycles, provided the arrangement does not constitute unapproved offshore borrowing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after each anniversary of the company's incorporation date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 30% late-filing penalty on the prescribed fee; persistent non-filing for two consecutive years triggers removal from the companies register (administrative strike-off) under section 82 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the end of the company's financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-payment penalty plus prescribed-rate interest on unpaid tax; fixed-amount administrative non-compliance penalty of up to ZAR 250 per day for continuing failure to file.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: First Provisional Tax Return and Payment (IRP6)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the commencement of the financial year (interim estimate)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 20% underestimation penalty on the tax shortfall plus prescribed-rate interest on the deferred amount.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Second Provisional Tax Return and Payment (IRP6)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Not later than the last day of the company's financial year (year-end estimate)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 20% underestimation penalty on the tax shortfall plus prescribed-rate interest on the unfunded liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the financial year where taxable income exceeds ZAR 20,000
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Prescribed-rate interest and 20% understatement penalty for a substantial underpayment of the top-up liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Recurring two-month cycle, due on the 25th day after the end of each cycle; annual vendor review applies if VAT registration threshold of ZAR 1 million taxable turnover is met
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-payment penalty plus prescribed-rate interest; additional administrative penalties under section 210 of the Tax Administration Act for late filing or under-declaration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit is compulsory where the Public Interest Score (PIS) exceeds 350; where PIS is 100-349 an independent review is required unless the financial statements are independently compiled; PIS below 100 (typical for a single-shareholder DTC e-commerce entity) permits internally prepared annual financial statements subject to shareholder approval.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or IFRS for SMEs per Financial Reporting Standards Council recommendations; South African Statements of GAAP (SA GAAP) are no longer applicable for Companies Act reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual return declarations must confirm current beneficial ownership under the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022; any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be reflected in the register of members and the beneficial ownership register and notified to CIPC within 30 days of the transfer event.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023 (reduced from 28% for the 2022 year); assessed on worldwide income of a South African tax-resident (Pty) Ltd.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_doctrine: The Income Tax Act s 20 allows assessed losses to be carried forward indefinitely; no 5-year sunset applies. The schema code '5' is retained as a pipeline-comparability marker. Since years of assessment commencing on or after 1 April 2022, s 20A caps the utilisation of an assessed loss at 80% of taxable income per year; losses incurred in the first two years of formation are restricted unless the company actively trades (s 20(1) proviso).
